lists.title: Qualifications and designations
lists.about: Dentists in India hold a BDS (Bachelor of Dental Surgery, a five-year course that includes a compulsory internship) and may hold an MDS (Master of Dental Surgery) in one of the recognised specialities. Qualifications print on prescriptions and the clinic profile, so a consistent list avoids "BDS,MDS", "B.D.S" and "bds" all appearing for the same thing.
lists.admin_note: Store as a pick list with multi-select. Keep a free-text "other" for fellowships and certificates.

values.label: Fellowship
values.description: For example FICOI, FAGE (write the full name in the note)

lists.title: Dental specialities
lists.about: The Dental Council of India recognises nine MDS specialities, which the clinic profile and the patient app show next to a doctor's name. The nine below are given from general knowledge and a college-prospectus cross-check; confirm the names against the current DCI MDS regulations before publishing them. Many practices also advertise focus areas that are not recognised specialities (implantology, aesthetics), so the list has a second group.
lists.admin_note: Keep the nine recognised specialities as a locked group. Let the clinic add practice focus areas.

Names are examples to prompt the question, not a full drug list.

lists.admin_note: Show tobacco-related habits as a group with a prompt to examine the mouth and offer counselling.

values.label: Betel quid or paan (with or without tobacco)

lists.title: Tooth numbering (FDI)
lists.about: India uses the FDI two-digit system. The first digit is the quadrant: 1 upper right, 2 upper left, 3 lower left, 4 lower right (5 to 8 for the same four quadrants in children). The second digit counts from the midline: 1 central incisor, 2 lateral incisor, 3 canine, 4 and 5 premolars, 6 to 8 molars. Primary teeth have five per quadrant, so 1 to 5. So 36 is the lower left first molar, and 55 is the upper right second primary molar. The Universal system numbers permanent teeth 1 to 32 from the upper right third molar and primary teeth A to T; it is shown here only to help when an X-ray or report uses it. Store the FDI code.
lists.admin_note: Locked reference list. Use it to validate input: 19, 29, 39, 49 and 56 do not exist. Support a list ("12, 14, 16") by storing each tooth as its own row.

lists.title: Tooth surfaces
lists.used_in: Surface on a chart entry (not stored yet)
lists.about: A tooth has up to five surfaces. Write them as letters after the tooth number, for example 36 MOD means the mesial, occlusal and distal surfaces of the lower left first molar. Mesial faces the midline of the arch, distal faces away from it. Posterior teeth chew on the occlusal surface; front teeth cut on the incisal edge. Buccal is the cheek side, labial the lip side, facial covers both, lingual is the tongue side (lower teeth) and palatal the palate side (upper teeth); many clinics write L for both.
lists.admin_note: Locked reference list.

values.label: Occlusal
values.description: Chewing surface of premolars and molars

values.label: Incisal
values.description: Cutting edge of incisors and canines

values.label: Furcation
values.description: Between the roots of a molar

lists.title: Cavity classes (G.V. Black)
lists.used_in: Procedure names such as Composite Class 1
lists.about: Dr G.V. Black classified cavities by where they sit. Restoration procedures and material use depend on the class, which is why the usage rules in the brief are written as Class I and Class II. Class VI was added later.
lists.admin_note: Locked reference list; link each class to a default procedure.

values.label: Class I
values.description: Pits and fissures: occlusal of premolars and molars, buccal and lingual pits of molars, lingual pit of upper incisors

values.label: Class II
values.description: Proximal surfaces of premolars and molars (MO, DO, MOD)

values.label: Class III
values.description: Proximal surfaces of incisors and canines without the incisal edge

values.label: Class IV
values.description: Proximal surfaces of incisors and canines including the incisal angle

values.label: Class V
values.description: Cervical third (near the gum) of facial or lingual surfaces of any tooth

values.label: Class VI

lists.title: Diagnosis groups (ICD-10 K00 to K14)
lists.used_in: Diagnosis on a clinical note (not built)
lists.scope: Global, locked codes; clinic can add favourites
lists.about: ICD-10 Chapter XI groups diseases of the oral cavity, salivary glands and jaws as K00 to K14. These are the blocks; each has finer codes below it (for example K02.1 caries of dentine). Many clinics use plain names in daily work and map to ICD only for insurance or reporting. The WHO also publishes an ICD application for dentistry and stomatology; ICD-11 exists but ICD-10 is still the common reference in Indian clinics.

lists.title: Biomedical waste colour categories
lists.about: From Schedule I of the Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, 2016, as read for this study. Yellow: human and animal anatomical waste, soiled waste, expired or discarded medicines, chemical waste, chemical liquid waste, laboratory waste, contaminated linen. Red (contaminated recyclable plastic): tubing, bottles, IV sets, catheters, urine bags, syringes without needles or with fixed needles, gloves. White (translucent, puncture-proof, leak-proof, tamper-proof): waste sharps including metal such as needles, scalpels and blades. Blue: broken or discarded contaminated glass including medicine vials and ampoules, and metallic body implants. The Schedule does not name amalgam or extracted teeth: mercury and lead waste are dealt with under their own rules (Rule 7(11)), and extracted teeth are commonly treated as human anatomical waste (yellow). Confirm with the State Pollution Control Board. The dental examples in the notes are practical readings, not legal text.
lists.admin_note: Locked. Clinics may add local pickup details but not rename or merge categories.

lists.title: Retention periods
lists.used_in: Retention job (not built; hygiene photos only today)
lists.stored_today: Hygiene photos 90 days (setting); login codes 10 minutes
lists.scope: Platform defaults, clinic can lengthen not shorten
lists.about: How long each kind of data is kept. Clinical records: the Dental Council code of ethics, as quoted by the Indian Dental Association, asks for at least three years from the start of treatment, and the IDA recommends longer (it mentions eight years). Tax and accounting records are usually kept for several years by law; the figure depends on the law and the situation, so ask the accountant. DPDP asks that data be erased when its purpose ends unless the law requires it to be kept, so each category needs a recorded reason.
lists.admin_note: Table of data type, minimum, default, legal basis note. A job flags records past the period and deletes only if no legal hold applies.
